thread:
Alex (eng-infra): FYI - rolling driver 535->537 into staging-us-west this morning produced a small spike in GPU Xid errors and a couple NCCL watchdog restarts. Canary pool alerted. Anyone seen similar in other regions?

Maya (SRE): Thanks — saw the same. Alert went off around 10:02 UTC: a burst of Xid 43 and Xid 65 across 4 nodes. NCCL watchdog restarts correlated within ~20s.

sre-bot: ALERT: HighGpuXidRate fired (rule=HighGpuXidRate, severity=warning)
  - labels: region=us-west, pool=canary-gpu
  - expr: `sum by(code) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total{pool="canary-gpu"}[5m])) > 3`
  - firing at 2026-03-18T10:02:12Z

Devon (infra): Quick sanity: rolling diff was the kernel+driver combo (kernel 5.15.0-rc4 + driver 537.21). We bundled it with an NCCL bump. Could be a kernel-driver compatibility edge.

Samir (oncall): Mitigation steps I ran in staging: cordoned the 4 nodes, restarted nvidia-driver DaemonSet, and restarted affected pods. That stopped further Xid spikes. Kept node kubelets up to avoid full reboots.

Maya (SRE): Logging pattern: `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` shows repeated rebinds and then `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43` followed by some `nvidia-modeset` messages. NCCL logs show `watchdog: aborting` and then group reconnect.

Alex (eng-infra): We need to tune alerts + update runbook. Right now the alert is noisy for small canary blips. Proposal: change evaluation window to 15m and require node_count > 5 or % of pool > 5%. Also add automatic runbook link + escalation to infra oncall for warning->critical.

Devon (infra): Agreed. Current prom rule (short version):
```
alert: HighGpuXidRate
expr: sum by(code, region) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total{pool=~"canary.*"}[5m])) > 3
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
```
Change to: `for: 15m` and wrap with `sum_over_time(...)` and a `count(node)` min threshold.

Inga (observability): I'll open a PR to alerting repo. Also add a synthetic metric to differentiate 'transient driver bind' vs 'kernel oops' by matching `Xid` codes and repeated count per node. Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/GPU/gpu-error-ops (will include heatmap + per-node traces).

Maya (SRE): Runbook updates we should include: immediate triage checklist, mitigation play (cordon/drain, restart nvidia-driver DS, kubelet restart if needed, escalate to infra if >10% of pool), how to rollback driver safely (kubectl rollout undo ds/nvidia-driver -n kube-system or revert AMI for onprem), and who to page.

Samir (oncall): Command snippets from staging:
`kubectl cordon ip-10-0-22-45.us-west-2.compute.internal`
`kubectl drain ip-10-0-22-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
`kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver`
`# if still unhealthy, revert to driver 535 image: kubectl set image ds/nvidia-driver nvidia-driver=registry/redwood/nvidia-driver:535 -n kube-system`

Alex (eng-infra): Important: don't mass-reboot across AZs at once. We should gate driver rollouts by canary success for 24h and add automated rollback if Xid rate > threshold in prod. Also add a temporary mute rule for non-prod pools to reduce noise.

Inga (observability): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/alerting/pull/892 (contains rule change, new grafana panels, runbook link).

Maya (SRE): I'll edit the runbook page (docs/internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-upgrades.md) with the mitigation steps above + decision matrix (when to rollback vs when to patch kernel). Suggestion: add a smoke test after upgrade that runs `python tests/gpu_smoke.py` that allocates memory, runs an nccl allreduce, and checks for Xid emissions for 10m.

Devon (infra): We'll also add automated tainting for nodes that show >2 Xid errors in 10m so schedulers don't keep placing jobs on flaky nodes. Taint key: `redwood/gpu-fault=true:NoSchedule`.

Alex (eng-infra): OK plan summary: 1) Inga PR merges for alert tuning+dashboards, 2) Maya updates runbook + smoke test, 3) Devon implements taint automation + rollout gate, 4) Samir runs guarded rollback in staging if next canary shows Xid > threshold. Follow-up sync tomorrow 09:30 PT.

Samir (oncall): I'll also add a small note in the oncall rota to check GPU alerts during the next driver window. :thumbsup:

Maya (SRE): Thanks all — filing a short post-checklist ticket for post-rollout verification and tagging this thread.

sre-bot: NOTE: thread tagged `gpu-upgrade` `priority:medium`

Alex (eng-infra): Great. If anyone hits a hard regression before morning, @channel — escalate immediately.
